sections.heading: Slope compensation
sections.text: Peak current-mode flyback operating above 50% duty in CCM is subharmonically unstable without slope compensation. Add an artificial ramp with slope at least half of the inductor down-slope reflected to the primary. Insufficient slope compensation appears as period-doubling on the current waveform, which evaluators may misread as a tuning problem.

sections.heading: Voltage-loop bandwidth
sections.text: Place the outer voltage-loop crossover at approximately fsw/10 to fsw/5 in DCM. In CCM, the right-half-plane zero — frequency proportional to load and (1 - D)^2 — typically caps voltage-loop crossover at one quarter of the RHPZ frequency.

sections.heading: Leakage and snubber interaction
sections.text: Primary leakage inductance produces a voltage spike that is sensed alongside the legitimate switch current. If the controller acts on the spike, the duty-cycle command oscillates. Apply leading-edge blanking on the current sense long enough to clear the leakage transient before the loop sees it.

sections.heading: Mode transition
sections.text: DCM-to-CCM transition changes the small-signal model from a single-pole system to a double-pole-plus-RHPZ system. Pick the operating-point worst case (typically heavy load in CCM) for stability margin verification, and accept that DCM small-signal margin will be much larger.
